name: Install unknown apps
plain: Lets the app install other apps from APK files.
meaning: The gateway for sideloaded malware. Android makes users approve each source app; Play restricts the permission.

android.prompt_ui: Settings toggle: Install unknown apps, per source app
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Special app access > Install unknown apps
android.store_policy: Play: restricted; apps must declare core purpose of installing packages
android.note: Android 8.0 (API 26) replaced global Unknown sources with per-app permission.

ios.store_policy: Only in the EU under DMA marketplaces and web distribution (iOS 17.4)
ios.note: iOS has no sideloading by default; the EU opened alternative marketplaces in iOS 17.4.

limits.headline: Can install other apps from files on Android, only if you allow it for that app
limits.user_action: You open an app file and switch on Install unknown apps for the app that opened it
can: Install an app from a file after you allow it for that source
Show you a system confirmation before each install
Do this on iPhone in the EU through approved marketplaces, with a system confirmation
cannot: Install apps if you have not allowed Install unknown apps for it
Install silently; the system always asks you
Do this on iPhone outside the EU, which has no side loading by default
limits.reach_label: Only per app, after you allow it
limits.differs: Android has a per app switch since version 8. iPhone has no side loading by default; the EU opened alternative marketplaces in iOS 17.4.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app install other apps from files, so it can act like an app store.

marketing.name: Install unknown apps
marketing.pitch: Google explains that people must allow each source app before it can install apps from files.

story.for_you: When you open an app file from a browser, Android asks you to allow that browser to install unknown apps. You can switch it off per app later.
story.for_makers: Makers of app stores and company app tools need it. It is also the favorite door for malware, so Google restricts which Play apps can ask for it.

use_cases.example: A web browser downloads an app file and asks to install it.
A game store app installs a game outside of Google Play.
A company tool installs private work apps on staff phones.
An open source store installs apps you choose.
A fake update pops up and tries to install a malware app.
A banking trojan asks for this to drop more malware.
A tester installs a debug app from a download link.

story.android_note: Since Android 8, you allow it per source app instead of one global switch.
story.ios_note: iOS has no sideloading by default. The EU opened alternative stores in iOS 17.4.

history.change: Per-app Install unknown apps replaced the global toggle
Alternative app marketplaces enabled in the EU
